findings.title: Package heat partition is still an implementer choice
findings.section: U2 - Add physical solids and heat partition (physical thermal model)
findings.why_it_matters: An implementer can choose four independent neck solves or a combined package solve without a binding criterion, even though the existing runner performs independent per-neck solves. That leaves the bridge loss split and shared package coupling open to duplication or omission while still satisfying the listed tests. Require a source-bound power partition and an explicit joint-solve rule, with an INDETERMINATE result whenever the partition cannot be established.
evidence: U2 approach: 'finite thermal paths into the package and surrounding board'
U2 test 5: 'Bridge power is allocated once across sink/lead paths; no independent source is duplicated in four per-neck solves.'
U2 verification: 'If joint package coupling requires one combined four-lead solve, implement it explicitly.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a mandatory input-contract decision for package coupling: either run one combined four-neck/package solve, or provide a reviewed proof and numeric partition that makes independent solves valid. Missing or unbounded partition data must keep applicability INDETERMINATE and block thermal ranking.

findings.title: Bridge loss evidence is not bound into replay
findings.section: R3 - Bind current and bridge dissipation to the actual circuit and waveform (physical thermal model)
findings.why_it_matters: The current harness binds thermal current to the PFC branch report, but the cooling contract still carries a free-standing 40 W value and no retained diode-loss or waveform artifact is named. A model can therefore claim actual-circuit binding while continuing to use an allowance that is not an upper bound. Add a hashed loss-evidence input and require production replay to recompute or reject it before any thermal ranking.
evidence: R3: 'Bind current and bridge dissipation to the actual circuit and waveform; distinguish RMS conductor heating from diode loss.'
Cooling U1 approach: 'Check the exact bridge diode behavior against the PFC current waveform.'
Shared baseline: 'Treat the 40 W bridge loss allowance as an assumption to check against the PFC waveform and exact-part behavior.'
findings.suggested_fix: Define a versioned, hashed bridge-loss evidence record (waveform, diode model/data, temperature/tolerance assumptions and integrated loss) and add it to the physical-model/cooling input contract. The production runner must bind that record to the board and recompute the loss-derived temperatures; absent or stale loss evidence is INDETERMINATE.

residual_risks: The cooling goal asks for a buildable arrangement, but the cooker-enclosure collision envelope and neighboring heat loads are not yet numerically defined; the plan should keep physical fit INDETERMINATE when those inputs are unavailable rather than selecting on the 170 x 160 x 95 mm module allowance alone.
deferred_questions: What reviewed evidence will establish the bridge package's heat split to the case, leads, solder and each of the four necks, or authorize a mandatory combined solve?

resolution_verification.finding: Package heat partition is still an implementer choice
resolution_verification.evidence: Physical-model KTD6 now mandates one shared package network coupled to all four lead paths and the sink, forbids four independently heated package replicas, and keeps unknown package-path parameters INDETERMINATE. U2 verification now requires the coupled package/lead energy contract and global residuals.

resolution_verification.finding: Bridge loss evidence is not bound into replay
resolution_verification.evidence: Physical-model KTD7 names a versioned loss-input record with exact MPN, datasheet bytes/curve, junction-temperature range, tolerances and the PFC waveform report. U1 supplies that record, while U3 requires production binding, Rust recomputation and a mutation test for diode curve, waveform, weighting and package heat.

resolution_verification.finding: Cooling physical fit could be overclaimed
resolution_verification.evidence: Cooling U1 continues to record missing enclosure dimensions as uncertainty, and R7/Definition of Done distinguish calculated suitability, physical fit and qualification. The plan therefore does not promote the module allowance to a collision-checked fit claim.
